forces.title: AI adoption transforms real estate operations and value creation.
forces.description: The real estate sector is undergoing a profound shift with the widespread adoption of AI. Historically playing a peripheral role, AI is now becoming integral across the project lifecycle, from planning and construction to sales and asset management. This transformation enables more coordinated decision-making, improved capital efficiency, and enhanced transparency, fundamentally reshaping how value is generated and sustained in commercial and mixed-use real estate.

forces.title: Rising GCC activity drives significant office space demand.
forces.description: Global Capability Centres (GCCs) are a primary driver of office space absorption in India. Foreign firms leased a record 9.1 million sq. ft. of office space in Q1 2026 across top nine cities to set up GCCs. Overall, GCC leasing surged 24% YoY to 31.8 million sq. ft. in FY25, accounting for 42% of pan-India office absorption. This ensures robust demand, rental appreciation, and continued development of new business districts in commercial hubs.

forces.title: Growing retail real estate demand from brands and new supply.
forces.description: India's retail market is experiencing strong leasing activity, with approximately 8.9 million sq. ft. leased across major cities in CY25. This demand is fueled by the expansion of fashion and apparel brands, direct-to-consumer (D2C) players, and food and beverage operators. The top 7 Indian cities are expected to add nearly 9 million sq. ft. of new retail space in 2025, supported by a rising supply of quality retail developments like malls and high-street outlets.

forces.title: Evolution towards performance-driven real estate ecosystems and active ownership.
forces.description: The real estate industry is undergoing a structural reset where value creation is shifting from mere capital allocation to superior operating performance. Success in the next cycle will hinge on active asset selection, design, operation, and rotation, rather than just acquiring assets. This involves adapting to vibrant property ecosystems that combine residential and commercial elements, industrializing construction, elevating facility management, and integrating AI to maximize asset performance and avoid obsolescence.

forces.title: Real estate lags other sectors in AI adoption and maturity.
forces.description: Despite the significant value AI can unlock, the real estate sector lags the global average in AI maturity by approximately 15%. This gap is attributed to a conservative culture, asset-heavy operations limiting standardization, and historically strong returns reducing the urgency to modernize. Limited AI investment, forecasted at 0.8% below the cross-industry average in 2026, is expected to widen this adoption and maturity gap, posing a competitive disadvantage for commercial real estate players.

forces.title: Persistent project overruns and inefficiencies plague real estate development.
forces.description: Real estate projects are structurally exposed to significant inefficiencies, with 66% experiencing schedule overruns and 39% facing cost overruns. Drivers include fragmentation, rework, misaligned stakeholder incentives, supply chain volatility, and limited standardization in project delivery. These issues contribute to lower margins and increased volatility, highlighting the urgent need for technological intervention and process improvements to mitigate risks in commercial and mixed-use property development.

forces.title: Government digital reforms enhance transparency and investor confidence.
forces.description: The Indian government is acting as a digital catalyst, implementing initiatives like geo-referenced land parcels, integration of sub-registrar offices with revenue systems, and verified property documents through the National Blockchain Framework. These reforms aim to improve transparency, strengthen title certainty, reduce disputes, and lower structural risks. Such digital foundations are creating a genuinely investment-ready real estate ecosystem, particularly benefiting institutional participation in commercial properties.

forces.title: SEZs becoming key extensions of real estate business, attracting investment.
forces.description: Special Economic Zones (SEZs) are increasingly viewed as extensions of the real estate business, attracting significant investment and employment. With 368 notified SEZs in India and total investment reaching ₹7.86 lakh crores by December 2025, they offer substantial opportunities. The allowance of 100% FDI for townships within SEZs further enhances their appeal, particularly for office and business park developers seeking strategic locations and driving the overall growth of commercial real estate.

forces.title: Modern building techniques driving productivity gains in construction.
forces.description: Construction excellence is becoming a key differentiator, particularly for large ecosystem deliveries including commercial and mixed-use developments. Modern techniques such as modular construction, robotics, and digital twins are enabling significant productivity gains. While developed countries have seen stagnation, emerging markets like India have benefited from these advancements, unlocking an estimated $1.6 trillion in annual value worldwide by improving project speed, ensuring consistent quality, and enhancing scalability across real estate construction.

forces.title: Infrastructure-led public spending creates new real estate growth corridors.
forces.description: The Union Budget 2026-27's sharp focus on infrastructure, with a significant increase in public capital expenditure (INR 12.2 lakh crore), will stimulate real estate growth. Investments in transport networks, urban infrastructure, and the development of seven high-speed rail corridors will unlock new growth corridors. This particularly benefits commercial and retail developments by expanding economic centers beyond traditional metros and into Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, driving incremental demand across various asset classes.

forces.title: Institutional investments and REIT expansion boost liquidity and transparency.
forces.description: Institutional investment in India's real estate market remained resilient, with significant inflows. The REIT sector surpassed a Rs. 1,00,000 crore market capitalization in November 2025 and is projected to expand up to US$123 billion by 2029, driven by institutional demand in office and retail assets. The RBI permitting banks to lend to REITs and proposed REITs for CPSE-owned assets further enhance liquidity, long-term financing, and the overall transparency of the commercial real estate market.

forces.title: Flex space and co-working models reshaping office market demand.
forces.description: The rise of co-working and flexible office spaces is transforming the office market dynamic. India's flexible office space supply is expected to surpass 80 million sq. ft. by end-2025. Operators leased 2.24 lakh seats across eight major cities in 2024, driven by corporate demand for flexible, scalable, and cost-effective solutions. This trend influences demand for both traditional and smaller office spaces, making flexibility a key offering and strategic consideration for office developers.

forces.title: ESG performance and decarbonization becoming critical for real estate value.
forces.description: Environmental sustainability is no longer just compliance but has significant financial implications for commercial real estate. Assets without net-zero plans face 'brown discounts' of 10-15%, and lenders/insurers are factoring climate performance into loan terms. Green bonds and sustainability-linked loans now represent over $500 billion annually in real estate financing, offering lower costs and access to capital. Decarbonization strategies, particularly in operations and materials, are crucial for competitive advantage, rental premiums, and exit valuations.

viewpoints.title: Technology now essential for India's real estate value creation and capital access.
viewpoints.description: India's real estate market, projected to reach USD5.8 trillion by 2047, is undergoing a fundamental transformation where technology is no longer a differentiator but a condition for accessing capital and building trust. The sector needs to re-think operations across the full project lifecycle, with AI adoption in corporate real estate rising from under 5% in 2023 to 91% in 2025. This shift emphasizes transparent, technology-driven platforms for institutional investment in commercial and mixed-use environments.

viewpoints.title: Infrastructure-led budget boosts real estate, especially commercial and retail.
viewpoints.description: The Union Budget 2026-27, while lacking direct housing incentives, sets a constructive backdrop for real estate through infrastructure-led growth. Increased public capital expenditure and focus on urban development, manufacturing, and tourism will create strong indirect momentum for commercial, industrial, and hospitality segments. Emphasis on Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, along with high-speed rail corridors, will unlock new growth corridors and drive incremental demand across various real estate asset classes.

viewpoints.title: AI offers significant value uplift despite real estate's current low maturity.
viewpoints.description: Real estate is structurally inefficient, with 66% of projects facing schedule overruns and 39% cost overruns. AI capabilities are now mature enough to address these issues, offering 400-700 bps margin uplift for development companies and 200-300 bps EBIT uplift for facility management. Despite lagging the global average in AI maturity by 15%, the sector has a clear opportunity to transform operations, reduce costs, and enhance revenue through strategic AI adoption, particularly relevant for mixed-use properties and office automation.

viewpoints.title: Real estate's future success depends on active ownership and operational excellence.
viewpoints.description: The real estate sector is undergoing a structural reset, moving from a capital-allocation-driven model to one where operational performance dictates value. Future success will be won by those who 'operate best,' not just 'buy well.' Firms must adapt to the rise of vibrant commercial ecosystems, industrialize construction, elevate facility management, and integrate AI to maximize asset performance and avoid margin compression and asset obsolescence, particularly impacting office markets.

viewpoints.title: Indian real estate poised for substantial growth driven by urbanization and demand.
viewpoints.description: India's real estate sector, the second-highest employment generator, is projected to reach US$5-7 trillion by 2047, potentially surpassing US$10 trillion. Institutional investment remained resilient in Q1 2026, with domestic demand driving nearly three-fourths of inflows. Rapid urbanization, with 900 million Indians expected in urban areas by 2047, ensures sustained demand. The office and residential segments are attracting significant capital, reinforcing investor confidence in the sector's long-term growth.
